spiritual_reading.full_translation:
Before obscurity and illumination were distinguished within the whole created order, a sufficient mediating power was called forth. Afterward that mediating power was directed into the outermost emptiness and disorder, so that wisdom might be purified there and so that obscurity and illumination might be separated from each other.

Before wisdom was loosed from restraint and rose through that lowest region, the Divine source of living good prepared for it ordered receptive forms in the inner degree. These were established so that wisdom might be cleansed within them and brought into determinate form and harmonious arrangement.

Before evil had multiplied into dominion in the outer human life, and before those in good and those in evil were distinguished from one another, the principle of just discernment was sent forth and made manifest. The seat of that discernment was fixed within a living spiritual medium, so that judgment might proceed in justice, and so that the good and the evil might be examined, proved, and separated according to what they are.

Again, before the human race came into actual existence, states were already allotted, and some were foreseen as abounding in spiritual resources while others were foreseen as lacking them in the outer degree. Before the end of their worldly life, those who would remain in spiritual death were marked out by prevailing external patterns that seem to order life and by persuasive appearances that govern in the natural mind. Such determinants were assigned to them, and within them their first formations were established. Their inmost tendency was entangled with these persuasions, and they were driven by them toward an equalizing judgment according to their works and their evils.

Again, before the present ordered state is brought to its end, the forces that serve dissolution are designated and instructed for that final loosening.

And before a renewed state could be established, perfected, and set in distinct form, the governing power of formation was summoned, together with the primary ordering intelligence and the ministering powers that work with it, to build and bring that new state into beauty and order.

Afterward that mediating power was directed into the outermost emptiness and disorder, so that wisdom might be purified there and so that obscurity and illumination might be separated from each other.
paragraph_translations.connection: OPENS the chapter’s sequence by establishing mediation prior to discernment of states.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Third Ambassador” treated as a mediating power of sufficiency; “void and outer waste” required reading as outermost disorder.

paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by showing the provision of inner forms that prepare wisdom for ascent.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Ships of light” forced into ‘receptive forms’ by function; exact nuance of ‘ships’ as doctrinal containers is inferred.

paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by introducing discernment that separates good from evil in a living medium.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Flesh” read as outer human life; “living atmosphere” as a spiritual medium sustaining judgment.

paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS to foreseen allotments and external determinants that drive toward judgment.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Stars/zodiac/sphere” required a functional rendering as external patterns and persuasive appearances; ‘births’ rendered as first formations. The passage mixes providential foreseeing with deterministic compulsion, which strains the voice.

paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES the ‘beforehand appointment’ theme, now focused on ending an age.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Destroyers” treated as permitted destructive forces under direction; brief and schematic.

paragraph_translations.translation: And before a renewed state could be established, perfected, and set in distinct form, the governing power of formation was summoned, together with the primary ordering intelligence and the ministering powers that work with it, to build and bring that new state into beauty and order.
paragraph_translations.connection: CLOSES by turning from dissolution to the formation of a renewed state.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Great Builder/first architect/angels” translated by function; “new aeon” as renewed state of the church/order.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: The chapter is coherent as a single teaching about prior appointment: mediation before discernment, preparation of receptive forms before ascent, judgment before moral separation is enacted, foreseen allotments before embodied life, dissolution before renewal, and rebuilding before the new state appears. Coherence is strongest in the first, second, fourth, and final movements. The only stumble is the deterministic tone of the ‘stars and zodiac’ paragraph, which presses external compulsion more than the surrounding providential ordering, but it still fits the theme of externals governing those who remain in spiritual death.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential opening: a functional sequence (summons → sending → purification → separation) that sets the chapter’s ‘beforehand appointment’ logic without administrative cataloguing.
findings.evidence: Text: “before night and day were differentiated… the Third Ambassador was summoned… sent… that he might purify the light, and separate night and day.” The spiritual reading reports no narrative break here and can render “Third Ambassador” as “mediating power” by function (mediation that enables differentiation). The sense arises from what is done (purify/separate), not from jurisdictional rank.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly correspondential substrate; imagery is functional but metaphorically opaque (“ships of light”), causing minor strain without indicating insertion. The passage continues the same process-logic (preparation of vessels → purification → shaping) and does not introduce governance lists.
findings.evidence: Text: “Father of Life made… the ships of light… so that it might be purified in them, and be sculpted and fashioned in good order.” The reader notes being “forced” to construe ships as “receptive forms,” but that is a normal metaphorical difficulty: the functional telos (“purified… sculpted… fashioned”) is explicit and matches the chapter’s process narrative. Removing it would *harm* coherence (it is the step between sending/purifying and later judging/separating).

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential/judicial development: judgment is introduced as a function needed before moral sorting. Although it uses institutional terms (“Judge,” “throne”), it still teaches by function (testing/separating) rather than by enumerating administrative jurisdictions.
findings.evidence: Text: “the Judge was sent forth… His throne was created… so that… the righteous and the sinners would be set apart and tested and separated.” The spiritual reading smoothly integrates it as “principle of just discernment,” with “living atmosphere” as sustaining medium. The governing nouns (“Judge/throne”) do not become a roster of powers; they serve the functional verbs “set apart… tested… separated,” preserving the narrative’s internal logic.

findings.diagnosis: Insertion into a functional narrative: deterministic astrological administration intrudes (stars/zodiac/sphere appointing births and compelling outcomes). The voice shifts from prior functional provisioning/judgment to external governance by cosmic officials/signs, forcing the reader into allegorization and producing the chapter’s only reported stumble.
findings.evidence: Text: “they who will die are marked out by the stars and the signs of the zodiac in the sphere. They are appointed for them; in them are their births… bound up with their zodiacal signs; and they are compelled by them…” The spiritual reading explicitly flags strain: “required a functional rendering… mixes providential foreseeing with deterministic compulsion, which strains the voice.” That strain is best explained textually as a layer concerned with astral determination (who is assigned/marked/compelled) rather than correspondential function. If the astrological lines are skipped, the paragraph can read as a simple ‘pre-allotment’ motif consistent with the surrounding sequence (“before mankind… named rich/poor… brought to judgement”), with far less forcing.
findings.scope: “Before they die, they who will die are marked out by the stars and the signs of the zodiac in the sphere. They are appointed for them; in them are their births. And their root is bound up with their zodiacal signs; and they are compelled by them and brought to an equal judgement in accordance with their deeds and their sins.”

findings.diagnosis: Schematic but coherent continuation of the ‘prior appointment’ sequence. The destroyers are introduced only as functionaries of dissolution, without names/ranks; brevity alone is not evidence of overlay.
findings.evidence: Text: “the destroyers were appointed and instructed for its dissolution.” The spiritual reading notes it as “brief and schematic” yet it continues the same temporal framing (“Again, before…”) and functional outcome (dissolution) that pairs naturally with ¶8’s rebuilding.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly correspondential closure with mild administrative coloring: building the new aeon is taught through functional roles (build/make beautiful), though the triad “Great Builder… first architect… angels” edges toward rank language. It does not, however, become an inventory of jurisdictions, and it completes the dissolve→renew arc.
findings.evidence: Text: “Great Builder… first architect and the angels… who would build and make beautiful the new aeon.” The spiritual reading can translate by function (“governing power of formation… ordering intelligence… ministering powers”), indicating the passage still supports correspondential interpretation. It also restores narrative balance after ¶7 (dissolution vs construction).

textual_criticism.summary: 6 findings: 1 clear disruption (¶6) where an astrological-determinist administrative layer intrudes into an otherwise correspondential sequence of beforehand provisioning (mediation → vessels → judgment → dissolution → rebuilding). Recommended: 1 excision (the zodiac/stars compulsion block), 0 annotations, 5 no-action confirmations. The rest of the chapter reads as a coherent functional narrative; the only reported ‘stumble’ aligns with the voice shift and is best explained as insertion rather than genuine difficulty.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Know that before night and day were differentiated in the universe, the Third [Am]bassador was summoned. And afterwards, he was sent to this void and outer waste that he might purify the light, and separate night and day from each other.

⟨p.117⟩ Before the light was released and freed and ascended through this zone, the Father of Life made beautiful for it the ships of light. He constructed them so that it might be purified in them, and be sculpted and fashioned in good order.

[Bef]ore Sin had multiplied and had made a kingdom in the flesh, before the acquitted and the condemn[ed] were set apart from each other, the Judge [w]as sent forth and revealed. His throne was created and placed [i]n the living atmosphere, so that he would be a just Judge, so that there the righteous and the sinners would be set apart and tested and separated from each other.
Again, [befo]re mankind had been engendered, some were named ['rich' and] others 'poor' on earth [and the fate was set] upon them.
Again, before the universe is dissolved, [and the] entire earth, the destroyers were appointed and instructed for its dissolution.

And before the ne[w] aeon was [built and] made be[auti]ful and marked out, [the] Great Builder [w]as summoned, the first architect and the angels who are with him, who would build and make beautiful the new aeon.

changes_summary: Applied Finding 4 (¶6) excision: removed the astrological-determinist block about stars/zodiac marking births and compelling outcomes (“Before they die… in accordance with their deeds and their sins”) as an intrusive administrative layer. No other paragraphs were changed per Findings 1–3 and 5–6 (recommendation: none).
